bib.title: DS-1000: A Natural and Reliable Benchmark for Data Science Code Generation

read.skipped: Appendix figures 16-31 (example problems) skimmed by caption only; they are prompt/code examples

question: How can a data science code generation benchmark use natural StackOverflow problems yet have reliable execution-based evaluation and resist memorization?
hypothesis: Models may answer public problems by recalling pre-training solutions, so perturbing problems without raising difficulty should expose and prevent this.
contributions: 1000 realistic problems over seven Python libraries from StackOverflow
multi-criteria evaluation (test cases plus surface-form constraints) with 1.8% false discovery rate
proactive perturbation against memorization, with a numpy-100 pilot

method.summary: Authors hand-adapted 451 StackOverflow problems into 1000 problems with executable code contexts, test cases and surface-form constraints, perturbing more than half to differ from the web source. Five code models were evaluated with pass@1 from 40 samples per problem.
method.task: data science code generation (infilling and left-to-right completion)

datasets.name: DS-1000
datasets.source: StackOverflow, 7 libraries (Pandas 291, NumPy 220, Matplotlib 155, Scikit-learn 115, SciPy 106, PyTorch 68, TensorFlow 45)
datasets.preprocessing: filter: >=1 vote, >=1000 views, accepted answer, deduplicated; stratified by year for Pandas/TensorFlow; random initial pool of 4500; rubric-ranked; 152 surface perturbation, 235 semantic perturbation, 162 difficult rewrite, 451 origin

datasets.name: numpy-100
datasets.preprocessing: code context written, one test case each, surface and semantic perturbations written manually

inference.temperature: 0.2 (benchmark); 0.7 for the 2800-sample reliability audit and numpy-100 pilot
inference.samples: 40 per problem (unbiased pass@1 estimator); numpy-100 pilot 10 samples x 20 problems; audit 40 samples x 70 problems
inference.prompting: zero-shot; Insertion (infilling with [insert] marker) or Completion (left context only, right context rewritten as instructions)

other.library_versions: Python 3.7.10; Matplotlib 3.5.2, NumPy 1.21.6, Pandas 1.3.5, Scikit-learn 1.0.2, SciPy 1.7.3, TensorFlow 2.10.0, PyTorch 1.12.1, Seaborn 0.11.2

metrics.name: pass@1
metrics.definition: unbiased estimator from 40 samples; sample passes only if all test cases and surface-form constraints pass

metrics.name: false discovery rate
metrics.definition: fraction of auto-accepted samples judged incorrect by annotators

eval.protocol: Single run per config; no seeds or significance tests stated. Reliability audited on 10 problems per library by manual review.

prompts.where: Fig 1 (insertion marker block; rest is problem text and code context)

results.note: Authors infer weaker memorization because StackOverflow items repeat less than numpy-100; indirect evidence only

limits: Memorization evidence on DS-1000 is indirect: perturbation drops are 3.4 and 9.0 points on subsets, not comparable to Table 5.
numpy-100 pilot uses only 20 problems, 10 samples and one test case each.
Reliability audit covers only Codex-002 on 70 problems; only 1.6 test cases per problem on average.
Several Table 6 cells average fewer than 10 problems (starred).
Single library versions fixed (2022); models are 2022-era.
Authors concede the cause of the gap between Codex and 6B models is not isolated (size, instruction tuning, pretraining data).
Matplotlib has no perturbed problems and only Completion format.
